organisation: Social Catalyst Lab, University of Zurich
proposal: Create a business and management extension that reuses APE's public-data paper-production corpus and execution conventions while Portsmouth supplies journal-readiness review, academic-time logging and portfolio weighting.
mutual_value: APE gains an independently governed institutional production-function study; Portsmouth avoids recreating a 1,000-paper generation and review infrastructure.
first_contact_goal: Discuss access to the APE paper/run schema, limits of the tournament judge and a jointly specified two-paper pilot.

proposal: Adapt CRED's defect taxonomy and cost-recall machinery to business and management papers, adding construct validity, identification and theory-evidence alignment as separately adjudicated domains.
mutual_value: CRED gains a discipline extension and human-guidance cost data; Portsmouth gains a tested mechanical verification layer.
first_contact_goal: Request the current CRED codebook, injected-error generator and verifier result schema; agree what can be reused without implying journal quality.

proposal: Share social and behavioural replication tasks as low-risk production-function cases and compare human-only, protocol-specified and method-autonomous conditions.
mutual_value: Adds priced human guidance and journal-output links to replication; gives Portsmouth human-verified replication tasks.
first_contact_goal: Identify two business or management compatible cases with public or redistributable inputs.

proposal: Reuse the progressive guidance-withdrawal design while recording academic minutes, model cost, rework and journal-readiness outcomes.
mutual_value: Tests whether ASI-Bench's guidance gradient transfers to social-science production; gives Portsmouth an established autonomy manipulation.
first_contact_goal: Align guidance-condition definitions and discuss cross-benchmark reporting.

proposal: Co-design a dry and damp organisational sandbox in which agents must distinguish prediction, causal identification and theory recovery.
mutual_value: Extends the sandbox framework beyond biology; gives Portsmouth exact-ground-truth scientific-reasoning diagnostics.
first_contact_goal: Agree the minimal specimen-assay-oracle interface for an organisational research world.

organisation: FAIR / University of Oxford RPM authors
proposal: Test whether pairwise research-branch selection and pilot experiments reduce cost per journal-ready business paper relative to more inference or more rollouts.
mutual_value: Provides a social-science portability test with direct resource accounting; gives Portsmouth an adaptive compute allocator.
first_contact_goal: Share a candidate-action schema and identify the smallest inference-only RPM comparison.

proposal: Adapt question-specific criteria into blinded reviewer packs calibrated to journals represented in Portsmouth's actual portfolio.
mutual_value: Provides a demanding domain transfer and human calibration study; gives Portsmouth scalable but bounded rubric generation.
first_contact_goal: Compare criterion-generation outputs with two academic reviewers on one paper challenge.

proposal: Replicate the seven human-intervention modes on business and management article production, replacing generic human involvement with timed academic work packages.
mutual_value: Extends intervention evidence beyond machine-learning research; gives Portsmouth tested candidate conditions for human-compute substitution.
first_contact_goal: Obtain exact intervention definitions and run-ledger fields.
